# ReflectiveLoop

A literature-review knowledge base for self-improving agent harnesses, skills, and systems, following the LLM Wiki pattern. This branch contains **22 PDF-grounded papers**, with source notes, synthesis pages, and research questions.

Start with the [generated catalog](index.md), [overview](wiki/overviews/self-improving-llm-agents.md), [mechanism comparison](wiki/concepts/procedural-self-improvement.md), and [evaluation boundaries](wiki/concepts/evaluating-self-improvement.md).

## Added September 18, 2026

- [EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning](wiki/self-improving-agents/huang-2026-envharness-awakening-static-worlds-for.md) ([arXiv:2608.19880v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19880v1)) — Adapts resettable environments to diagnosed policy weaknesses through initial-state replay and interaction wrappers while retaining native verifiers. Skill and RL gains on original held-out tasks add an environment-adaptation axis to the wiki, with explicit transfer and compute limits.

## Added September 16, 2026

- [Stellar Colosseum: A Many-Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Research in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science](wiki/self-improving-agents/lin-2026-stellar-colosseum-a-many-agent.md) ([arXiv:2609.15983v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15983v2)) — Readiness-gated proof planning, overlapping candidate-and-critique aggregation, and localized repair with persistent research memory. An inference-time harness comparator; learning the controller or model remains future work.

## September 12 user-requested additions

- [Auto-RecSys](wiki/self-improving-agents/li-2026-auto-recsys-harnessing-autonomous-research.md) — Persistent industrial research agents with evolving playbooks; operational adaptation evidence and explicit limits on validation and transfer.
- [Ecdysis](wiki/self-improving-agents/yue-2026-ecdysis-efficient-and-effective-training.md) — Cross-task failure aggregation and diagnostic refinement before harness edits; frozen model-transfer tests and qualified accuracy/cost claims.

Published in [PR #6](https://github.com/DrSquare/ReflectiveLoop/pull/6), stacked on [PR #5](https://github.com/DrSquare/ReflectiveLoop/pull/5), preserving the pending seed-PDF and literature updates. See the [September 12 review log](logs/2026-09-12-codex-workspace.md) and [September 13 publication log](logs/2026-09-13-codex-workspace.md).

## September 11 scan additions and upgrades

- [Experience Funnel](wiki/self-improving-agents/gao-2026-experience-funnel-a-state-policy.md) (September 8) - Alternating state evolution and policy consolidation; a direct comparator for the research question, with reporting caveats.
- [HarnessCompass](wiki/self-improving-agents/zhang-2026-harnesscompass-guiding-automatic-harness-evolution.md) - Constrained harness search with independent task holdout and frozen-harness cross-model tests.
- [AutoHarness](wiki/self-improving-agents/lou-2026-autoharness-improving-llm-agents-by.md) - Generated action verifiers or complete code policies; environment-specific rather than learned editor transfer.
- [AutoSaddler](wiki/self-improving-agents/park-2026-autosaddler-automatic-harness-optimization-with.md) - Exact-PDF upgrade of the entry on main, correcting offline-learning interpretation and narrative arithmetic.

## Earlier September 11, 2026 UTC additions

- [SkillAdam](wiki/self-improving-agents/li-2026-skilladam-stable-and-efficient-skill.md) — SkillAdam uses persistent issue history and an adaptive edit budget to stabilize optimization of natural-language skill documents around frozen models.
- [SE-GoS](wiki/self-improving-agents/fu-2026-se-gos-self-evolving-graph.md) — SE-GoS evolves the graph and descriptions used to retrieve existing skills, while preserving skill content, model weights, and the retrieval algorithm.
- [SkillForge](wiki/self-improving-agents/yang-2026-skillforge-evolving-verifiable-skills-for.md) — SkillForge makes skill invocation explicit in agent trajectories and revises skills using usage outcomes while training the policy with GRPO.
- [Prime Agent](wiki/self-improving-agents/karten-2026-prime-agent-a-self-improving.md) — Prime Agent packages a persistent REPL, recursive agent sessions, and versioned harness state into a runtime for long-horizon reasoning and execution.
- [Evo-Harness](wiki/self-improving-agents/wei-2026-evo-harness-context-to-harness.md) — Evo-Harness compiles failed one-shot task executions into reusable general and task-type guidance for a frozen solver operating on a task stream.
- [SESA](wiki/self-improving-agents/fu-2026-self-play-meets-skill-evolution.md) — SESA couples search self-play to an evolving skill bank, allowing skill-conditioned learning to improve both model parameters and optional inference-time memory.
- [Self-Harness](wiki/self-improving-agents/zhang-2026-self-harness-harnesses-that-improve.md) — Self-Harness uses the same frozen model to solve tasks and propose bounded changes to its own harness, with regression scores deciding which edits survive.
- [Life-Harness](wiki/self-improving-agents/xu-2026-adapting-the-interface-not-the.md) — Life-Harness turns training-trajectory failures into reusable runtime interventions and freezes the resulting harness for held-out evaluation across model backbones.
- [MCE](wiki/self-improving-agents/ye-2026-meta-context-engineering-via-agentic.md) — MCE evolves the instructions and code that build context, then executes those skills to produce context artifacts, while keeping model weights frozen.
- [Darwin Godel Machine](wiki/self-improving-agents/zhang-2025-darwin-godel-machine-open-ended.md) — The Darwin Godel Machine evolves a population of coding agents that modify their own implementations, retaining useful stepping stones under empirical evaluation.

The four original papers are Meta-Harness, Hyperagents, SIA, and CoSkill. Their PDF-grounded corrections are preserved from PR #2. PR #4 merged into the PR #2 branch; AutoSaddler merged into main through PR #3. The latest scan is stacked on the current seed-PDF branch and upgrades AutoSaddler under its existing stem. PR #2 remains open; this scan does not merge PRs.

## Daily scan

A ChatGPT task is configured for **08:00 America/Los_Angeles every day**, including daylight-saving changes. It searches primary sources, checks duplicates across the catalog and open PRs, adds exact PDFs and substantive notes, updates synthesis, validates the wiki, and publishes an ingestion PR. Following the user's September 13 instruction, it automatically merges eligible scan PRs into the default branch after validation, required checks/reviews, and mergeability checks pass. Conflicts, unresolved findings, missing PDFs, and unmerged dependencies block merging; existing draft/stacked PRs #2 and #5 remain untouched. The existing task was re-enabled, with the next scheduled date September 14. See the [scan procedure](agenda/llm-wiki-ops/daily-paper-scan.md) and [scan state](agenda/llm-wiki-ops/scan_state.json). No API key or GitHub Actions runner is required by this repository configuration; the scheduled task uses the connected research and GitHub tools.

## Add or validate papers

Follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), then run:

```bash
python3 scripts/build_index.py --apply
python3 scripts/validate_wiki.py
```

The [PDF manifest](papers/manifest.json) records versions and provenance. The [scan report](logs/reports/2026-09-11-literature-scan.md) records coverage, evidence qualifications, and pending work. All wiki content is English.

# EnvHarness implementation provenance — September 18, 2026

Operational repository observations are kept outside paper-grounded wiki evidence.

- Official repository: https://github.com/google-research/envharness (also linked by PDF p. 1).
- Inspected default-branch commit: `fab7d57441f06b75c73a900e04561d4d7600f361`.
- The public README exposes experiment drivers for ALFWorld, WebArena, SWE-bench, OfficeQA and SpreadsheetBench, plus an RL folder. This is availability inspection, not successful reproduction.
- The PDF calls its operators Stage/Contract/Chain and maps them to Setups/Rules/Link in Appendix A. The inspected repository README uses Setup/Rules/Link. Keep paper terminology in evidence notes.
- README defaults use an OpenAI model, while paper tables use Gemini. A code default is not a reproduction of the paper setting.
- Frozen-backend and reusable-interface claims do not establish a hardened security sandbox, arbitrary mid-episode rollback, or correctly verified semantic composition.
- No external README claims are used as scientific evidence in sources/wiki beyond the paper-linked official-code provenance.

## One-line Summary

EnvHarness improves the experience available to an agent by wrapping a resettable environment with initial-state replay, interaction transformations, and task composition; a fixed designer loop targets observed policy weaknesses, and skills or RL policies learned from the adapted environments are evaluated on untouched tasks.

## 2. Key Contributions

The optimization target is the environment-facing experience rather than just the agent's prompt, weights, or skill text. External wrappers modify how the policy encounters an existing task without replacing its native scorer. EnvRigger supplies task- and policy-conditioned wrapper proposals from success/failure traces, with fresh rollouts before acceptance. This supplies a concrete environment-adaptation baseline for research on evolving skills and agent improvement. [PDF §§2-3, pp. 4-7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=4)

Evidence covers skills extracted on five benchmarks, a separate Qwen RL experiment on two environments, and iterative skill accumulation on SWE-bench. These are distinct protocols: the main autonomous pipeline excludes task chaining, cross-model experiments regenerate the adaptation process per model, and the designer's own update procedure is fixed. [PDF pp. 8, 10-11, 19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=8)

## 3. Methodology and Architecture

### Environment wrappers and their boundaries

- **Stage:** run a saved list of legal actions after reset and before the policy begins. This changes the initial state through reachable transitions, making a missing subskill necessary or pre-completing earlier subgoals. Preparation counters can be rewound via `notify_replay_complete()`. Reproducibility assumes a deterministic reset. [PDF pp. 5-6, 23](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=5)
- **Contract:** transform or block actions before execution, rewrite the environment response, or filter observations. Hooks read a data-only state view, rather than browser/container runtime handles. Rewriting a returned response is not the same as changing the native simulator's internal transition function. Terminal verification remains delegated to the base environment. [PDF pp. 5, 19, 22-23](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=23)
- **Chain:** combine two environments into a longer episode with a shared step budget. In the evaluated serial version, the second leg resets lazily at handoff; outcomes are cached and composite success is the conjunction of the two native verdicts. A composite objective therefore differs from one base task, even though its component verifiers are reused. [PDF pp. 5, 23](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=23)

Layers share the same interface and can nest, but order matters: replay under an inner restriction need not produce the same state as replay followed by that restriction. The abstract contract includes `reset`, `step`, `observe`, `evaluate`, `get_env_state`, `save_state`, and `from_state`. Each benchmark still needs an adapter and a schema/prompt describing its tools and state. [PDF pp. 6, 19, 21-23](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=21)

Persistence is deliberately weaker than arbitrary rollback. In-memory environments may serialize live state; browser/container backends may retain only reset arguments, making restoration valid at episode boundaries. This is relevant to enterprise evaluation and RL: a resettable sandbox can use replayed initial conditions, but a live account with irreversible effects does not meet the paper's assumptions. [PDF pp. 22, 41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=22)

### EnvRigger and the learning loop

1. Collect five baseline policy rollouts on a training task.
2. Diagnose weaknesses and choose whether to simplify or make the task harder. Both successes and failures inform this choice.
3. Emit a candidate action-replay list and/or Python interaction hooks. The number of components is not capped.
4. Evaluate the candidate using five fresh rollouts. Use aggregate success, failure categories and timeout counts to accept, reject or refine; allow at most five write/validate rounds. A rejected instance can yield no component.
5. Extract reusable skills from the resulting experience, or use adapted environments for RL. In the scaling study, later environments target the policy with its accumulated skills.

This is an LLM-guided acceptance process based on a small rollout sample, not a proof of solvability or causal diagnosis. Its operating mechanism and externally supplied objective are fixed. Generated code runs in an episode subprocess for fault isolation; that description alone does not establish a security boundary. [PDF pp. 6-8, 19, 23, 26](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=19)

### Skill-learning protocol

Designer, policy and skill extractor use the same backbone: Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite on ALFWorld/WebArena and Gemini-3.5-Flash elsewhere. ReasoningBank-style extraction/retrieval is held constant. Each test instance is attempted once; reported main-table results are means over three independent runs with standard deviations. Training and testing use disjoint episodes; **test environments are original and unreshaped**. [PDF pp. 8-9, 25](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=25)

| Benchmark | Training/adaptation corpus | Evaluation as reported |
|---|---|---|
| ALFWorld | 100 standard training tasks | Remaining held-out tasks; official seen/unseen configurations |
| WebArena | 20 tasks per subdomain | Remaining tasks |
| SWE-bench | 100 Lite tasks | 407 Verified issues not in Lite |
| OfficeQA | 50 official training tasks | 172 official test tasks |
| SpreadsheetBench | 100 of 400 verified tasks | 299 tasks / 897 instances |

Table 7 does not account explicitly for the one-task difference between 400 minus 100 and 299; preserve the reported denominator rather than silently changing it. Spreadsheet Pass@1 aggregates base tasks, whereas Mean Score averages instances. Baselines match seed tasks, environment counts, model and extraction/retrieval pipeline; this does **not** imply equal total tokens or wall time. [PDF p. 25](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=25)

## 4. Key Results and Benchmarks

### Skills evaluated on untouched tasks

Values below compare skills from original environments with skills from adapted environments. Differences in success metrics are percentage points. [PDF Tables 2-3, p. 9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=9)

| Metric | Original environments | EnvHarness | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ALFWorld average success | 62.4 ± 3.4 | 68.3 ± 1.3 | +5.9 |
| ALFWorld OOD success | 61.4 ± 4.3 | 70.4 ± 2.3 | +9.0 |
| WebArena average success | 38.5 ± 3.1 | 41.6 ± 1.8 | +3.1 |
| SWE-bench Verified success | 49.88 ± 2.59 | 52.58 ± 2.72 | +2.70 |
| SWE-bench average steps | 55.01 ± 1.69 | 49.61 ± 2.49 | -5.40 steps |
| OfficeQA EM | 54.40 ± 1.84 | 56.20 ± 2.34 | +1.80 |
| OfficeQA F1 | 55.77 ± 1.59 | 57.73 ± 2.29 | +1.96 |
| SpreadsheetBench Pass@1 | 45.88 ± 1.19 | 49.15 ± 0.36 | +3.27 |

The headline 9.0-point gain is ALFWorld OOD, not an average across benchmarks. The 9.8% step reduction is `(55.01 - 49.61) / 55.01` on SWE-bench, relative to original-environment skills; relative to no skills (53.58 steps), the reduction is about 7.4%. Table 3 labels the step improvement +5.40 in the beneficial direction; the signed change is -5.40. Standard deviations are not confidence intervals or significance tests.

### RL is useful but does not improve every split

Qwen3-8B-base is trained with GRPO separately on original versus adapted environments. ALFWorld In-Dist rises **81.4 → 87.9**, OOD falls **89.6 → 88.8**, and the average rises **85.5 → 88.4**. WebShop score rises **75.6 → 79.2** and success **66.0 → 67.4**. The 6.5-point maximum is ALFWorld In-Dist. Calling the 0.8-point OOD decline statistically negligible is unsupported by a reported uncertainty analysis. [PDF Table 4, p. 10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=10)

The stated recipe uses 8 H100s, vLLM, FSDP/offloading/checkpointing, 4096 prompt tokens, 512 response tokens, 50-step episodes, temperature 0.4, invalid-action penalty 0.1, and seed 0. Appendix F reports 150 epochs/steps, global batch 16 and PPO minibatch 256; effective batching and the epoch/step equivalence should be reconciled with runnable configuration before reproduction. Table 4 supplies no multi-seed variance. It also does not isolate whether the environment pool is regenerated online at each policy update. [PDF pp. 26-27](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=26)

### Scaling, task transfer, and chaining

- **Iterative skills:** at 300 environments and 15 accumulated skills, SWE success reaches 54.79 versus 52.13 for original environments and 50.37 for SWE-smith. Each 50-environment batch adds a bank; environment count/retrieval are matched, not necessarily end-to-end compute. Some round-three tasks exhaust the candidate budget without accepted changes, limiting an unqualified compounding claim. [PDF pp. 11, 31-32](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=11)
- **Across models:** SWE gains over original-environment skills are 3.2 points on Flash-Lite, 3.7 on Qwen3.6-27B, 2.7 on Flash and 3.2 on Sonnet 4.6. Each setting uses its own matching designer/policy model. This demonstrates applicability of the pipeline across models, not reuse of one frozen skill bank or wrapper set across model families. Average steps increase for three of the four adapted-vs-original comparisons; efficiency is model-dependent. [PDF pp. 11-12, 33-34](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=34)
- **Held-out task types:** ALFWorld leave-one-type-out average success rises 60.6 → 63.7; four types improve, one ties and heat declines 61.1 → 52.4 (-8.7 points). This narrows universal transfer claims. [PDF Table 10, p. 35](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=35)
- **Chain:** independently paired training tasks yield skills tested on standard single-environment SWE tasks. Chain-only gives 49.63% success / 41.96 steps; combining Chain and Stage/Contract skills gives 54.30% / 43.12. The main Stage/Contract result is 52.58% / 49.61. This supports complementary skill sources, but not verified autonomous generation of semantically linked cross-domain workflows. [PDF pp. 8, 10-11, 33](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=10)
- **Objective targeting:** on 100 ALFWorld tasks, measured with ten rollouts each, the fraction within a success band [0.4, 0.6] rises 6% → 80%; a successful-episode step band [25, 35] rises 18% → 53%. Band occupancy is not held-out task accuracy or a downstream-learning guarantee. [PDF Table 12, p. 36](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=36)

## 5. Limitations and Future Work

**Compute matching:** estimated ALFWorld totals are 228.0M tokens for EnvHarness versus 64.2M for GenEnv (about 3.55×); WebArena totals are 137.3M versus VeriEnv's 137.8M. The kinds of rollout differ (real execution versus GenEnv's simulated interaction), so neither equal environment counts nor lower deployment steps establishes uniform training-cost efficiency. [PDF p. 35](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=35)

**Reset and verification assumptions:** deterministic replay and restorable backends are prerequisites. Reusing a scorer preserves its implementation, not its completeness, absence of leakage, or all task semantics under arbitrary perturbations. These latter distinctions are this note's interpretation of the interface contract and examples. Appendix G includes response manipulation and source/test-file edits through ordinary actions; backend code staying fixed does not mean every task artifact or observation is immutable. Fresh rollout gates remain important. [PDF pp. 6, 23, 29-32, 40-41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=40)

**Scope of composition:** the interface and Appendix D illustrate branching/interleaving control flow, while experiments use serial conjunction and Appendix H/I explicitly lack a verified semantically shared composite objective. Do not turn expressible control flow into demonstrated arbitrary workflow verification. [PDF pp. 23-25, 41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=41)

**Attribution:** there is no full matched-compute factorial isolation of diagnosis, state replay, response shaping, candidate selection and skill extraction. Five validation rollouts make acceptance noisy. The unchanged designer procedure is not a learned or self-rewritten meta-improver; stronger across-task skill and cross-model portability require additional controls. Current observations/actions are textual, including the browser adapter. [PDF pp. 8, 19, 26, 35, 41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=19)

## Definition

Environment adaptation changes the experience an agent receives from an existing task through external state preparation and interaction wrappers. In [[huang-2026-envharness-awakening-static-worlds-for]], the native backend and scorer remain in place, while the start state, exposed actions and returned observations can change. This separates the learning environment from the held-out evaluation environment. [PDF pp. 4-8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=4)

## Mechanism

EnvRigger diagnoses successful and failed traces, emits replay actions and Python hooks, and accepts or revises candidates from fresh rollout statistics. Later adaptation can target the policy with its accumulated skills. This is policy-conditioned curriculum construction under a fixed designer procedure; it is not evidence that the procedure learns to rewrite itself. [PDF pp. 6-8, 11, 19, 26](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=19)

## Reset, composition and verifier boundaries

1. **Reset establishes reproducibility.** Stage replay assumes deterministic reset. A heavy runtime may store reset arguments rather than a full snapshot; its restoration guarantee then stops at episode boundaries. This does not supply transactional rollback for arbitrary state-changing actions. [PDF pp. 6, 22-23, 41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=22)
2. **Scorer reuse has a precise scope.** Keeping native evaluation code does not imply invariant observations, immutable task files, or complete coverage of every new failure mode. Generated hooks can fabricate response information and ordinary replay actions can modify task artifacts. Their training usefulness must be checked empirically. [PDF pp. 19, 29-32, 40](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=40)
3. **Serial verdict composition is limited.** Requiring both native tasks to pass yields a tractable composite verdict. Branching control flow alone does not define correctness for semantically related tasks sharing state or intermediate results. [PDF pp. 23-25, 41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=41)
4. **Evaluation should remain separate.** The paper adapts training instances and tests learned skills on original held-out tasks. Altering test interfaces while comparing agents would confound capability changes with changes to task difficulty. The latter statement is an experimental-design inference from the reported separation. [PDF pp. 8, 25](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=25)

## Implications for skill and RL experiments

For research on [[questions/does-a-modifiable-meta-procedure-improve-skill-library-co-training]], vary the experience source separately from the agent's editing/training rule. Compare static experience, fixed-designer environment adaptation, and any proposed learned meta-procedure using held-out original tasks and matched total budgets. Report per-task regressions, proposer/rollout costs, and success alongside episode length. These are proposed controls, not experiments established by EnvHarness. Its RL OOD decrease, task-type heat regression and unequal ALFWorld token budgets motivate them. [PDF pp. 10, 34-35](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=35)

For an enterprise sandbox, the paper supports an interface design worth testing: reproducible reset arguments, action replay for starting conditions, and native completion checks. Applying this interface to enterprise tasks would still require validated reset and completion semantics for each adapter. [PDF pp. 21-23, 41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=41)

## Connections

Paper: [[huang-2026-envharness-awakening-static-worlds-for]]. Overview: [[overviews/self-improving-llm-agents]]. This broadens the improvement taxonomy to include the environment supplying experience, while preserving the distinction between modifying that environment and learning a recursive improvement procedure.

## Summary
A growing line of work argues that a large fraction of an LLM
agent's usable capability lives outside the frozen model weights — in the
harness/scaffold, the meta-level procedure that modifies the agent, or the
skill library it draws on — and that these components should themselves be
learned or searched over, rather than hand-engineered once and frozen.
Twenty-two papers currently in this wiki cover different parts of that idea,
including the September 11 scans, the September 12 additions of Auto-RecSys and
Ecdysis, the September 16 addition of Stellar Colosseum, and the September 18
addition of EnvHarness.

Seed full-text review: September 8, 2026; all four seed PDFs are present.
Expanded review: September 11, 2026 UTC; all ten new PDFs are present. The
revisions below replace only interpretations changed or qualified by the
full text. See the [claim-change record](../../logs/reports/2026-09-08-seed-pdf-upgrade.md).

## Environment adaptation as an experience-source control

[[self-improving-agents/huang-2026-envharness-awakening-static-worlds-for]] adds an environment-side lever: replay reachable starting states and transform interactions around existing backends, while retaining native task verifiers. A fixed EnvRigger designer targets policy weaknesses; skill extraction or RL changes the downstream agent. Held-out evaluation returns to original tasks. This broadens the improvement taxonomy without establishing that the improvement procedure itself evolves. See [[concepts/verifier-preserving-environment-adaptation]] for reset, persistence and composition boundaries. [PDF pp. 4-8, 19, 21-23](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=6)

ALFWorld skill OOD success rises 61.4 to 70.4%, but the separate RL experiment's OOD result falls 89.6 to 88.8%. Cross-model experiments rerun adaptation per model; they do not transfer one frozen skill bank. Separately induced Chain skills help single-task SWE evaluation, but demonstrated chaining uses serial conjunction of native verdicts. Estimated ALFWorld token cost exceeds GenEnv's, so equal environment counts do not imply equal total budgets. These findings strengthen environment adaptation as a comparator and narrow blanket transfer/efficiency claims; the [[questions/does-a-modifiable-meta-procedure-improve-skill-library-co-training]] question remains open. [PDF pp. 9-11, 34-35, 41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=10)

## Research-state refinement as an inference-time comparator

[[self-improving-agents/lin-2026-stellar-colosseum-a-many-agent]] adds a designed
workflow that improves the current proof and its supporting research state:
strategy readiness gates precede dependency-aware decomposition, candidate
critiques survive overlapping aggregation, and localized verifier findings
support section repair or renewed exploration. A knowledge directory retains
useful results and failed routes with evidence and caveats. This broadens the
comparison beyond changing harness code or weights; refining an artifact is
not itself evidence of a learned or self-editable improvement procedure.
[PDF §§4.1-4.3, pp. 6-9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.15983v2#page=6)

Its 71.0% TCS-Bench result uses selection between two harness runs, with a
reference-assisted automated grader. Its proof-to-Codeforces adaptation adds
a terminal C++ implementation task and execution probe, obtaining 218/222
accepted programs against hidden final tests. These are different validation
regimes, and neither comparison isolates orchestration benefits at matched
compute. Adaptive allocation and model training from validated trajectories
are proposed future work. Thus the paper strengthens the case for retaining
structured negative feedback during long tasks, while leaving the
[[questions/does-a-modifiable-meta-procedure-improve-skill-library-co-training]]
question unanswered.
[PDF §§6-8, pp. 13-17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.15983v2#page=13)

## Seed papers

- [[self-improving-agents/lee-2026-meta-harness-end-to-end]]

- [[self-improving-agents/zhang-2026-hyperagents]] (Hyperagents /

  from joint paper-review/robotics runs to math grading, not among all

- [[self-improving-agents/hebbar-2026-sia-self-improving-ai]] (SIA) —

## Cross-cutting observations from the seed review
- All four treat some component that is conventionally hand-designed once
  and left static (harness, meta-modification procedure, or skill
  workflow) as an object that should itself be optimized during training
  or deployment.
- Meta-Harness and SIA are mechanistically related, but not a matched
  head-to-head experiment. SIA explicitly discusses Meta-Harness and
  Hyperagents and reports prior comparator scores. Yet its LawBench
  setup describes 191 classes and solution-script rollouts, versus
  Meta-Harness's 215-class description. SIA also describes using test-split
  scores as RL feedback. Its incremental gains therefore do not establish
  independent generalization superiority over Meta-Harness.
  [SIA, §§4.1, 6.1-6.3, pp. 4, 8-9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.27276v2#page=9);
  [Meta-Harness, §4.1, p. 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.28052v1#page=6)
- Hyperagents and CoSkill expose different improvement mechanisms:
  editable meta-agent code versus a learned skill-editing policy under
  fixed training rules. Combining them is a plausible research hypothesis,
  not demonstrated compatibility or superiority. Hyperagents' transferred
  meta-agent is frozen during imp@50, and both task and meta code are
  carried over. Its 200-iteration transfer advantage (0.640 vs 0.610) is
  not statistically significant. CoSkill reports separate environment
  training, not cross-environment editor transfer.
  [Hyperagents, §§5.2-5.3, pp. 9-13](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.19461v1#page=9);
  [CoSkill, §4, pp. 6-9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.04865v1#page=6)
- Evidence of transfer must be separated from optimization against a
  benchmark: Meta-Harness holds out classification/math problems, but
  uses the same 89 TerminalBench-2 tasks for search and final evaluation.
  Its math experiment evaluates five models, only four of which were
  absent from search. CoSkill's main baselines largely use prior reported
  values, with protocol ambiguities documented in its source note. The
  four papers do not support a common controlled performance ranking.
  [Meta-Harness, §§4.2-4.3, pp. 8-9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.28052v1#page=8);
  [CoSkill, Table 1 and Appendices E-F, pp. 7, 19-20](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.04865v1#page=7)

## Interpretations changed by the expansion

**Learning the procedure is already a concrete research direction.** MCE evolves the skill that constructs context, and DGM lets coding agents improve their own implementations. The broad proposal to optimize an improvement procedure is therefore insufficient as a novelty claim. The remaining question concerns what joint editor/reasoner training and controlled cross-environment transfer add beyond these mechanisms. [MCE, pp. 5-7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.21557v2#page=5); [DGM, p. 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.22954v1#page=4)

**Persistent improvement has several substrates.** SkillForge and SESA change skills alongside trained policies. SE-GoS instead changes retrieval topology, weights, and descriptions without editing the skill bodies. SkillAdam changes a skill document under a fixed stateful optimization rule. These should occupy separate cells in an experimental design. [SkillForge, pp. 4-6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24747v1#page=4); [SESA, pp. 3-5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.29468v1#page=3); [SE-GoS, pp. 5-7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.08228v1#page=5); [SkillAdam, pp. 5-7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.08944v1#page=5)

**Continued editing can hurt.** Evo-Harness reports degradation with self-generated feedback; SE-GoS drops after additional evolution rounds. SkillAdam's memory and bounded edits address a related stability problem, but its Adam analogy does not establish convergence. [Evo-Harness, p. 8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.15071v1#page=8); [SE-GoS, p. 10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.08228v1#page=10); [SkillAdam, pp. 6-7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.08944v1#page=6)

**Transfer evidence has different strengths.** Life-Harness freezes training-derived interventions before testing additional models. Self-Harness uses its held-out scores in edit selection. SE-GoS provides a disjoint split but explicitly places its +5.4-point gain inside the noise band. Prime Agent's external ARC reference comparison is not a controlled harness-effect estimate. The expanded literature does not support a single performance ranking. [Life-Harness, p. 7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.22166v1#page=7); [Self-Harness, p. 7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.09498v1#page=7); [SE-GoS, p. 10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.08228v1#page=10); [Prime Agent, p. 7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.23552v1#page=7)

See [[concepts/procedural-self-improvement]] for mechanism definitions, [[concepts/evaluating-self-improvement]] for evaluation requirements, and [[questions/does-a-modifiable-meta-procedure-improve-skill-library-co-training]] for the narrowed research question.

## Question
Would combining Hyperagents' editable meta-agent
procedure with CoSkill's joint Meta-Skill-Agent/Reasoning-Agent RL
training outperform either approach alone?

## Sharper follow-up
Specifically: would an editable procedure for proposing, diagnosing, or
selecting CoSkill-style skill edits improve adaptation to an unseen
skill-library environment under a matched budget? Changing the RL
objective itself is a separate, stronger intervention, not something
required by Hyperagents' reported mechanism. Hold external scoring and
test selection fixed to isolate the benefit of the editable procedure.
This is a proposed experiment, not an established finding in this wiki.

## What the knowledge base holds
- [[overviews/self-improving-llm-agents]] — [[zhang-2026-hyperagents]]
  tests transfer from joint paper-review/robotics runs to math grading.
  During imp@50, the transferred meta-agent is fixed while it generates
  new task agents. Both task and meta implementations are transferred,
  and main parent-selection/evaluation rules remain fixed. This is not
  an all-pairs transfer experiment or a self-rewriting RL optimizer.
  [§§3, 5.2, pp. 5, 9-11](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.19461v1#page=9)
- [[feng-2026-coskill-joint-reinforcement]] jointly trains reasoning and
  editing roles in one shared actor. Its fixed protocol stages local
  edits, verifies them by task replay, and updates weights with GiGPO.
  Removing editor RL removes its objective, not all shared-weight
  adaptation. Separate ALFWorld/WebShop runs do not test editor transfer.
  [§§3-4 and Appendix G, pp. 3-9, 20](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.04865v1#page=3)
- Neither paper evaluates the other's setting, so there is no direct
  evidence in this wiki either way.

## Tentative answer
Unknown — no paper in this wiki tests this combination directly. This is a
candidate direction to flag if/when a paper explicitly combining
self-editable meta-procedures with skill-library co-training is ingested.

The full text narrows the analogy without resolving the question.
Hyperagents provides evidence for transferred agent-generation ability,
but its 200-iteration compounding endpoint is not significantly better
than initialization without transfer. CoSkill provides within-environment
co-training ablations, not cross-domain evidence. A clean test would
separately transfer the editor/procedure while holding task initialization,
total training and verification budgets, and test exposure constant.
These controls are this wiki's inference from the reported limitations.
[Hyperagents, §§5.2-5.3, pp. 10-13](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.19461v1#page=10);
[CoSkill, Table 2/Appendix F, pp. 8, 20](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.04865v1#page=8)

## September 11, 2026 UTC evidence update

The answer to the exact joint-training question remains unknown, but the novelty boundary is narrower:

- [[self-improving-agents/ye-2026-meta-context-engineering-via-agentic]] already evolves a reusable context-building procedure with a base executor and fixed model weights. Any claim of first learning the procedure behind skill/context construction must account for it. [pp. 5-7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.21557v2#page=5)
- [[self-improving-agents/yang-2026-skillforge-evolving-verifiable-skills-for]] makes invocation observable and maintains skills using outcomes, but its teacher/editor is fixed. This does not establish the proposed jointly learned meta-procedure. [SkillForge, pp. 4-6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24747v1#page=4)
- [[self-improving-agents/fu-2026-self-play-meets-skill-evolution]] adds an especially useful evaluation control: the same learned solver with memory disabled versus enabled. This separates deployment retrieval from gains carried in weights, although it does not alone isolate all training mechanisms. [p. 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.29468v1#page=6)
- [[self-improving-agents/li-2026-skilladam-stable-and-efficient-skill]] offers a strong fixed stateful editor, and [[self-improving-agents/fu-2026-se-gos-self-evolving-graph]] offers a retrieval-only adaptation control. Both are relevant alternatives to changing the learned editing policy. [SkillAdam, pp. 6-7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.08944v1#page=6); [SE-GoS, pp. 5-7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.08228v1#page=5)

A sharper proposed experiment compares a fixed learned procedure, a fixed stateful editor, an evolving procedure, and CoSkill-style joint training under matched total budgets. Transfer the editor separately from the skill bank and solver weights into a disjoint environment. Keep final task scores out of edit selection, measure negative transfer and repeated-update degradation, and include memory-off evaluation. These are research-design inferences from [[concepts/procedural-self-improvement]] and [[concepts/evaluating-self-improvement]], not claims that the combination is novel across all unreviewed literature.

## September 11 scan: consolidation baseline and stronger transfer controls

[[self-improving-agents/gao-2026-experience-funnel-a-state-policy]] is close prior art: it alternates validated textual-state evolution with policy consolidation on SearchQA, ALFWorld, and WebShop. Alternation, state-policy compatibility, and memory-free deployment can no longer serve as the proposed contribution by themselves. It does not establish a learned, self-editable editor or transfer of that editor into a disjoint environment. Reporting inconsistencies prevent treating its small gains as decisive quantitative evidence. [PDF pp. 3-7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.08919v1#page=3)

Add a fixed-editor alternating-distillation baseline, with both ordinary updated-state-success filtering and transition-aware weighting under the same rollout budget. Evaluate the full state, residual state, and no state with identical final policy weights. Cross transfer of the editor, bank, and policy independently; report adaptation curves on genuinely unseen environments, not merely independent training in several domains. This is a proposed design inference, not an established theorem or novelty guarantee.

Use [[self-improving-agents/zhang-2026-harnesscompass-guiding-automatic-harness-evolution]] as a constrained frozen-model harness baseline and [[self-improving-agents/park-2026-autosaddler-automatic-harness-optimization-with]] as a history-aware development-selection baseline. Their task/model holdouts strengthen the required evaluation standard but do not answer the learned-editor transfer question. ## September 18: environment adaptation as a separate control

[[self-improving-agents/huang-2026-envharness-awakening-static-worlds-for]] provides a fixed designer that adapts training environments to observed policy weaknesses while retaining native verifiers. Learned skills and a separate RL policy are tested on original held-out environments. Its designer procedure remains fixed; the skill and RL protocols do not jointly train a self-editable meta-procedure and skill-editor/reasoner pair. Thus it does not answer the combination question. [PDF pp. 6-10, 19, 26](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=8)

A further proposed control is to vary the experience source independently of the skill-editing/training rule: original environments versus fixed-designer adapted environments, using the same original held-out evaluation and matched total proposer, rollout and learning budgets. Report task-level regressions and independently transfer wrappers, skills, editor and policy. This is a research-design inference motivated by EnvHarness's RL OOD decline, task-type regression and unequal ALFWorld token budgets. [[concepts/verifier-preserving-environment-adaptation]] records the boundaries. [PDF pp. 10, 34-35](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=35)

## Summary

EnvHarness makes an existing resettable environment a policy-conditioned source of training experience. It changes initial conditions and interaction surfaces through wrappers; the native backend and task scorer are retained. EnvRigger diagnoses traces and validates generated wrappers, then agents improve through extracted skills or a separate RL training protocol. This evolves the experience source, while the designer's improvement procedure remains fixed. [PDF pp. 4-8, 19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=6)

## Key Contributions

- A common interface for reachable state preparation (**Stage**), action/response/observation transformations (**Contract**), and task composition (**Chain**).
- Black-box policy diagnosis with five baseline rollouts, five fresh rollouts per candidate, and at most five revision rounds. Whole candidate sets pass or fail together.
- Held-out evaluation on untouched tasks after learning from adapted training environments; separate tests of skill learning, RL, iterative skill accumulation, and model-specific application across four backbones.

The main autonomous skill pipeline uses Stage and Contract; Chain is separately constructed and evaluated. [PDF pp. 5-8, 26](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=8)

## Methodology and Architecture

Adapters expose reset/step plus observation, evaluation, a data-only state view, and persistence. Wrappers nest through the same interface, with noncommutative order. Stage replays actions after reset; Contract intercepts actions and returned information; serial Chain shares a budget, starts the second environment lazily and combines the two native success verdicts. [PDF pp. 5-6, 21-23](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=23)

Deterministic reset supports repeated validation of prepared states. Heavy runtimes may restore only at episode boundaries by rerunning reset arguments; this is not arbitrary state rollback and excludes non-resettable live accounts. A native scorer remains fixed, but the wrappers can alter information and task artifacts through ordinary actions, so verifier reuse alone does not certify all generated experience. [PDF pp. 6, 22-23, 40-41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=41)

In skill learning, designer, extractor and policy use the same model. Baselines match training seeds, environment counts and extraction/retrieval, and tests attempt original held-out instances once. Main results average three runs with standard deviations. SWE uses 100 Lite training tasks and 407 nonoverlapping Verified test issues; all benchmark splits are documented in the [source note](../../sources/huang-2026-envharness-awakening-static-worlds-for.md). [PDF pp. 8-9, 25](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=25)

[PDF Tables 2-4, pp. 9-10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=9). The headline +9.0 points is the skill-learning ALFWorld OOD result. The 9.8% reduction is SWE execution steps versus original-environment skills, not a reduction in total adaptation/training compute. The RL OOD decline has no supplied multi-seed uncertainty estimate.

At 300 environments, iterative SWE skill accumulation reaches 54.79% versus 52.13% from original environments and 50.37% from SWE-smith. Across four separately adapted backbones, EnvHarness skill gains are 2.7-3.7 points over original-environment skills; this is pipeline applicability, not transfer of a frozen bank between models. ALFWorld leave-one-type-out improves 3.1 points on average but loses 8.7 points on heat. [PDF pp. 11, 34-35](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=35)

Separately induced Chain skills yield 49.63% SWE success / 41.96 steps. Combining them with Stage/Contract skills gives 54.30% / 43.12, evaluated on ordinary single-environment tasks. This does not establish autonomous semantic workflow composition. [PDF pp. 10-11, 41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=10)

## Limitations

- Estimated ALFWorld token cost is 228.0M versus GenEnv's 64.2M; WebArena costs are close to VeriEnv (137.3M versus 137.8M). Environment-count matching is not all-in compute matching. [PDF p. 35](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=35)
- A five-rollout acceptance gate is fallible; a fixed scorer does not guarantee solvable or semantically faithful perturbations. Component contributions and diagnosis quality lack full factorial isolation. [PDF pp. 19, 26, 40-41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=26)
- Resettable text interfaces and benchmark adapters are prerequisites. Rich branching/interleaving is illustrated as control flow, but demonstrated composite verification is serial conjunction. [PDF pp. 21-25, 41](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=41)
- Preserve reported protocol ambiguities: SpreadsheetBench's 100 training plus 299 test tasks do not exhaust the stated 400; RL batching/epoch descriptions need reconciliation before reproduction. No experiment was reproduced here. [PDF pp. 25-27](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.19880v1#page=25)
